newsitem.title: UK: Trade group slams report on children's advertising.
newsitem.headline: Trade group slams report on children's advertising.

text.p: An advertising trade group on Monday called a recent critique of television advertising of food to children "deeply flawed", saying the report failed to put children's television viewing habits in context.

The report, A Spoonful of Sugar, was published earlier this month by the Consumers Federation, a consortium of consumer organisations from about 90 countries. It compared practices in 13 countries and found that confectionery, breakfast foods and fast-food adverts comprise more than 50 percent of all advertising in children's programming in the 13 countries surveyed -- including 12 western European nations and the U.S..
The Advertising Information Group criticised the report for failing to examine television advertising as but one of many influences on children's eating habits.

"The starting point of 'A Spoonful of Sugar' is deeply flawed in that it chooses only to consider advertisements in children's programming rather than to establish the real context of children's total viewing habits," the Advertising Information Group said in its monthly newsletter, AIG-Notices. "Thus is deliberately exaggerates what it claims are the influences of advertising in children's programming."
"There is nothing in this report to justify tougher restrictions on children's advertising," the trade group added.
